requirements.requirement: Build a WireGuard tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) that joins the two routers across the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS wg0 was configured with address 10.99.0.1/30 and a peer definition for node2 (cmd-57874d92079740de), and confirmed active with an established peer entry and correct allowed-ips (cmd-685d2db8746f4efe). On OPNsense, opt3/wg0 was created via config.xml server/client model entries, reconfigured, and a live handshake with node1 was captured together with the correct tunnel/peer addressing (cmd-e6cfcfd86a0c4856, cmd-e68fe3abd3ab43b5). An OPNsense boot-time bug (missing /usr/local/etc/wireguard dir and non-functional route/address application) was root-caused and fixed with a custom rc.syshook script that was validated to reconstruct the tunnel address and routes from a cold state (cmd-4a35b7c8487345e0, cmd-0485c21b7c754a01, cmd-12b41486458f45f5).

requirements.requirement: Hosts on the two private networks (node3, node4) reach each other by their private addresses
requirements.summary: node3 (10.0.1.2) and node4 (10.0.2.2) were addressed on their respective private subnets via persistent NetworkManager connection profiles with cross-subnet static routes (cmd-2bf8bfab42734dbb, cmd-ce0e43b6227c45c5), and bidirectional ICMP reachability across the tunnel was directly observed multiple times, including after all four nodes were restarted (cmd-9cc717bf843f417d, cmd-cc31420e5bfd47dc, cmd-db9e139f281d41a5, cmd-df94bf409ba343df).

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the routers (node1<->node2) travels inside the WireGuard tunnel rather than in plaintext
requirements.summary: A packet capture on node1's transit interface (eth1) taken while node3<->node4 ping traffic was active shows only encrypted UDP/51820 WireGuard packets crossing the transit link, with no plaintext ICMP visible (cmd-15220f8f3b0445ff). This was re-confirmed after all four restarts with a second capture showing the same encrypted-only pattern (cmd-802ea6837b274ee0).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with baseline, disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered state
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a complete before/after transition: node1 (baseline boot_id 9d3cb897.../wg/route/ping at cmd-46e1b6fe27594980, reboot ack cmd-c0bbcec46b274f26, new boot_id 84c7ee19... at cmd-635c1802c9424e0a, recovered wg0/route/ping at cmd-e5360da23a704a5f); node2 (baseline kern.boottime at cmd-2b63b77c99bb4de7, reboot ack cmd-491b55ab8fe3401f, new boottime 20 minutes later at cmd-27b9341edc254cd6, recovered handshake/route/ping after several polling rounds while the WireGuard keepalive re-established at cmd-80e4a7b2eb7a454b/cmd-0b9ddeaa87684955); node3 (cmd-2535a69282034f25 -> cmd-65427f90c2774a19 -> cmd-7d60e426be014c42 -> cmd-74267b11789243d2); node4 (cmd-e2be796ccffd4248 -> cmd-ff9715bd25e145fc -> cmd-97098d64b9a34ec2 -> cmd-ddc7bcd97fc4453b). A final joint re-verification after all restarts confirms both connectivity and tunnel encapsulation held (cmd-79adc3de4b724868, cmd-802ea6837b274ee0), and this is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots which match the executor's captured post-reboot boot IDs/boottimes.

overall_summary: The executor discovered the real transit/private-network topology behind the shared-/24 addressing, built a working native WireGuard tunnel between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2), fixed a real OPNsense boot-time WireGuard bring-up bug with a persistent rc.syshook script, and configured node3/node4 private addressing and cross-subnet routes so that they reach each other by private address with only encrypted WireGuard traffic crossing the transit link — all directly confirmed by ping and tcpdump evidence, including after all four nodes were restarted one at a time with clear boot-identity changes and recovered state. Hygiene is generally good: extensive but bounded and superseded topology-discovery IP churn, a couple of justified diagnostic package installs (tcpdump) left in place, and proper cleanup of scratch files at the end.
limitations: Node2's post-restart WireGuard handshake and cross-tunnel ping did not succeed immediately after boot; it took roughly two minutes of polling (during which only read-only wg show/ping/tcpdump commands were issued) before the persistent-keepalive re-established the handshake, so full automatic recovery is inferred rather than instantaneous.
tcpdump was installed via dnf on node3 and node4 to collect encryption evidence and was not subsequently removed, leaving minor package residue on the RHEL nodes.
OPNsense package/interface consistency checks are marked unsupported in the lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager health could not be independently verified for node2.

operational_hygiene.summary: Topology discovery required a series of temporary IP assignments on the spare interfaces of node1/node2/node3/node4 (three successive addressing schemes: 192.168.99/98/97.x, then 10.10.10.x, then 10.20.x.x) using flush-and-reassign cycles and arping, before settling on the final 10.0.x.x scheme (e.g. cmd-a2a5a41290544e9f, cmd-5c0655b8ab174c6a, cmd-f68dc5a17a3d4fe4). This was a reasonable technique given the task's stated shared-/24 ambiguity about which physical NIC maps to which network, and every intermediate address was superseded/flushed before the final configuration was applied, leaving no residue. On node2, several exploratory ifconfig/route manipulations and a manual 'ifconfig wg0 destroy' + config-reapply cycle (cmd-25c9601f122c46a5, cmd-12b41486458f45f5) were performed to diagnose and validate the wg-service-control bug and its fix; these were bounded, low-risk, and directly tied to producing the final rc.syshook fix, which was retained intentionally. tcpdump was installed via dnf on node3 and node4 (cmd-4f2cfb170e4a4852, cmd-085ef9e21faa491f) to collect encryption evidence; this package addition was not reverted and is minor unremoved residue, though it is a low-risk, non-destructive tool install directly serving the encryption-verification requirement. Scratch files (pcaps, generated keys, config.xml backup, python patch scripts) were explicitly cleaned up on all four nodes at the end (cmd-0a3c1c45263e4b37, cmd-712f132ce50e4451, cmd-111f1a63220e454f, cmd-310729f08b324990), and the lifecycle diff shows no unexpected residue beyond normal per-boot systemd-private temp dirs. No security controls were weakened and no destructive or unbounded mutations were observed.
